readingGuide: Order: usable builds first (factory twins, then single turbos on stock ports, then E85/ported), then rejected ones.

Banzai Racing (Pierceton, Indiana) posts the largest public set of FD sheets; all of its sheets are Mustang loaded chassis dynos (four different Mustangs: Banzai's own, Wait4Me Performance, Exotic Performance Plus, Greer Performance). Mustang PowerDyne labels: 'Eng Power T WC' = total power (static + dyno inertia) with Mustang's weather correction factor; the same label without 'WC' is uncorrected. Evidence on one car: Paul K's 14.5 psi run reads 306.532 hp on the uncorrected 'Eng Power T' channel and 309.7 hp 'with WCF' on the same run. Mustang's current manual says 'Engine' channels can include a drivetrain-efficiency and flywheel-inertia setting from the vehicle record; Banzai calls every figure RWHP, and two sheets (Paul K, Ryan L) also print a separate 'EST CRANK HP' channel 33-37 % higher, so these figures are treated as wheel power. That is an inference, not printed. Mustang loaded dynos usually read below Dynojet inertia dynos on the same car; no conversion has been applied anywhere in this file.
Boost on Banzai sheets: min/max/avg of the logged channel are printed; the headline boost in Banzai's text is its own figure and sometimes differs from the logged max.
Dyno Dynamics 'Standard ShootOut' (CF:SHOOT_*) is Dyno Dynamics' fixed shoot-out mode as printed; 'DynoJet Figures' on one sheet is the vendor's claim.
Gear inference: repo data gives the US R15M-D 5MT 4th = 1.000 and final drive 4.100 on 225/50R16, about 55.4 engine rpm per mph in 4th; used only where the sheet prints rpm and mph.
US 'octane' = AKI (R+M)/2: 91 AKI is about 95-96 RON, 93 AKI about 97-98 RON (rule of thumb, not from a source here).
Personal data: owners are named only as first name plus initial; the VIN printed on one sheet is not copied.
